$comment: Hand-written English meanings for the Concept noun of docs/DSL_KEYWORD_REFERENCE.md. A slot id is <def>.<property> (model.schema.json $defs) or pack:<property> / root:<property>. Only keywords whose schema node has no description are listed here (an entry here wins over a schema description). `inline` entries name keys written inside an inline object of a slot: <slot>.<key>. `defs` entries add a summary, a status and a minimal example to a $defs section.

concept.summary: A kind of record the app stores. A concept has fields, and optionally invariants, indexes, row-level access, events, a lifecycle (state machine), a composition (aggregate of child collections) and presentation hints. Each concept becomes a table, a REST resource and a generated screen.

field.summary: One column of a concept (and one entry of an object's properties). The `type` decides the stored shape; the remaining keywords add constraints, defaults, references, enum members and presentation.

domainType.summary: A reusable, named field type (for example an email address or a postal code): a base type plus validation, normalization and presentation that every field using it inherits through `field.domainType`.

enumOption.summary: A rich enum member, written instead of a plain string inside `field.enumValues` / `field.values` when the member needs a label, an icon, a badge or a position.

referenceDefinition.summary: The long form of `field.reference`: the target concept of a reference field plus how the generated UI looks it up, previews it and what happens on delete.

schemaObject.summary: A small inline type description (a JSON-Schema-like subset) used wherever a value is not a concept field: object and array shapes of fields, a domain type's validation, capability operation inputs and outputs, a flow's input and output schema and a procedure's returns. It is recursive through `properties` and `items`.

localizableLabel.summary: A text shown to users. Either a plain string, or an object with a required `default` text plus one entry per locale (for example `pt-BR`); the runtime picks the requested locale, then its language, then `default`.

presentationMetadata.summary: Presentation hints for the generated UI. Used on a concept (`concept.ui`: whole-list and whole-form behavior) and on a field (`field.ui`, `domainType.ui`, a panel field binding's `ui`: how the one field is labelled, grouped and edited). Hints only change how data is shown; they never widen access or change what is stored.

uiField.summary: The `ui` of a field or domain type: an alias of presentationMetadata.

conceptAccess.summary: Row-level authorization of a concept, evaluated per record: which rows a caller may read and which it may write, plus an optional anonymous public read grant.

index.summary: A database index over one or more fields of a concept, optionally unique.

invariant.summary: A rule every row of the concept must satisfy before it is written. Either a uniqueness rule over fields (`type: unique`) or a boolean expression over the row (`type: expression`). A specializing concept can replace an inherited invariant with `override: true`.

lifecycle.summary: The state machine of a concept: which field holds the state, the declared states and the allowed transitions between them.

lifecycleTransition.summary: One allowed move from a state to another, optionally guarded by an expression and tied to an event and a button.

actionMetadata.summary: How an action button is presented: caption, confirmation text, success and failure messages, danger level and visibility. Used on a lifecycle transition, a flow and a flow step.

composition.summary: Turns a concept into the root of an aggregate: a header plus owned child collections that are read and saved whole, in one transaction, at `/api/v1/runtime/aggregate/<Concept>`. Also holds the cross-collection rules (invariants, balances) and the hooks that run around a commit.

aggregateCollection.summary: One child collection of an aggregate: the concept it holds, the field that points back to the parent and, optionally, nested collections and read-only lookup columns.

aggregateCollectionLookupField.summary: A read-only column attached to every row of a collection when it loads, fetched from a declared query and joined in memory. Never persisted.

aggregateInvariant.summary: A named rule evaluated over the whole aggregate draft (root fields plus every collection) just before commit; a failure vetoes the commit and names the rule.

aggregateBalance.summary: A named balance rule over a collection whose rows are split into two sides by a discriminator field (for example origin and destination): per group, the summed quantities of the two sides must be equal, or the commit is vetoed.

sequence.summary: A document-numbering counter such as INV-2026-0001. A field takes the next value with `defaultExpression: "nextNumber('<name>')"`.

seed.summary: Rows inserted once, automatically, at first boot through the same governed save path as any other write. A seed is one record, or many (`count` / `repeatOver`).

slots.concept.name: The concept's name, unique within the model (PascalCase by convention). It names the table, the REST resource (`/api/<Concept>`) and every reference to the concept from queries, flows and screens.
slots.concept.specializes: Name of a base concept (usually contributed by a pack, written `pack::Concept`) that this concept specializes: it starts from the base's fields, invariants and events and may add to them. The base is pinned to the pack version the app was generated against (see `specializesFloat`).
slots.concept.truthLevel: The concept's declared verification maturity, `T0` (least) to `T6` (most). The release gate (`--releaseGate --targetTruthLevel=<T>`) refuses to promote a model whose concepts are below the target level.
slots.concept.module: Name of the bounded context (`modules[]` entry) this concept belongs to. Other contexts refer to it as `context::Concept`.
slots.concept.fields: The concept's fields, at least one. Field order is the default display order.
slots.concept.invariants: Rules every row must satisfy (uniqueness or boolean expressions). A violation rejects the write.
slots.concept.indexes: Extra database indexes (the platform already indexes ids and unique fields).
slots.concept.access: Row-level read and write rules, and an optional anonymous public read grant, for this concept.
slots.concept.events: Events declared inside the concept. A nested event with `mode` is published automatically by the generated create, update or delete.
slots.concept.lifecycle: The concept's state machine: status field, states and allowed transitions.
slots.concept.composition: Makes the concept the root of an aggregate whose child collections are read and saved whole.
slots.concept.ui: Presentation hints for the concept as a whole (labels, form layout, default grouping, offline writes).
slots.field.name: The field's name: its column name and its JSON key in the REST API. Unique within the concept.
slots.field.type: The stored type. `string`, `uuid`, `int` / `integer` (32-bit), `long` (64-bit), `decimal` (use with `precision` and `scale`), `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `enum` (needs `enumValues`), `reference` (to another concept's row), `object` (structured, described by `properties`), `array` (described by `items`), `file` (an uploaded file handle).
slots.field.id: When true this field is the concept's identifier (primary key). Conventionally a `uuid` field named `id`.
slots.field.required: True: a value must be supplied on create and may not be cleared. On an `object` field this may instead be a list of the property names that are required inside the object.
slots.field.unique: True: no two rows (within one tenant, and among non-deleted rows when the concept uses `softDelete`) may hold the same value.
slots.field.connectable: Set to `anchor` on a unique, non-id field to make it a natural-key anchor that other concepts may reference with `reference.via` (the foreign key then points at this field, scoped by tenant).
slots.field.enumValues: The allowed values of an `enum` field, in display order. Each entry is a plain string or an `enumOption` object that adds a label, icon, badge or order.
slots.field.ref: Shorthand for the target of a reference field: the name of the referenced concept. Prefer `reference`.
slots.field.reference: Makes the field a reference to another concept's row. Either the target concept's name, or a `referenceDefinition` object that also configures lookup, preview and delete behavior.
slots.field.domainType: Name of a `domainTypes[]` entry whose base type, validation, normalization and presentation this field inherits.
slots.field.description: A sentence saying what the field holds. Shown as help in the generated UI and read by AI authors.
slots.field.default: A literal value stored when the caller does not supply one on create.
slots.field.defaultExpression: An expression evaluated on create when the caller supplies no value, for example `nextNumber('invoice')`, `today()` or `$user.id`. Not re-applied on update.
slots.field.derivedExpression: An expression that computes the field's value from the row's other fields. The value is calculated by the platform, not supplied by clients.
slots.field.minLength: Minimum number of characters of a `string` value.
slots.field.maxLength: Maximum number of characters of a `string` value.
slots.field.min: Smallest allowed numeric value (inclusive) for `int`, `long` and `decimal` fields.
slots.field.max: Largest allowed numeric value (inclusive) for `int`, `long` and `decimal` fields.
slots.field.precision: Total number of digits of a `decimal` field (1 to 38).
slots.field.scale: Number of digits after the decimal point of a `decimal` field.
slots.field.minItems: Minimum number of elements of an `array` field.
slots.field.maxItems: Maximum number of elements of an `array` field.
slots.field.uniqueItems: True: the elements of an `array` field must all be different.
slots.field.itemIdentityField: For an `array` of objects, the property of each element that identifies it; used together with `duplicationPolicy` to detect duplicates.
slots.field.duplicationPolicy: For an `array` field: `allow` or `deny` elements that share the same identity (`itemIdentityField`).
slots.field.properties: For an `object` field, the structure: a map from property name to a `schemaObject` describing that property.
slots.field.items: For an `array` field, the `schemaObject` describing every element.
slots.field.ui: Presentation hints for this one field (label, placeholder, widget, grouping, visibility rules).
slots.domainType.name: The domain type's name, referenced by `field.domainType`.
slots.domainType.baseType: The stored type that fields of this domain type get (a scalar field type).
slots.domainType.validation: A `schemaObject` with the constraints (length, range, pattern, ...) applied to every field of this type.
slots.domainType.normalization: Names of normalizations applied to a value before it is validated and stored (for example `trim`, `lowercase`).
slots.domainType.format: A format hint for the value (for example an input mask or a well-known format name); also shown to users and AI authors.
slots.domainType.examples: Example values, used in generated help and in tests.
slots.domainType.ui: Presentation hints inherited by every field of this type.
slots.enumOption.value: The stored value of this enum member.
slots.enumOption.label: The text shown for the member (a plain string or per-locale object).
slots.enumOption.displayLabel: An alternative display text used where the short `label` is not enough, for example in a form dropdown.
slots.enumOption.order: Position of the member in dropdowns and filters (lower first). Members without `order` follow in declaration order.
slots.enumOption.group: Heading under which the member is grouped in dropdowns.
slots.enumOption.default: True: this member is preselected on create.
slots.enumOption.deprecated: True: existing rows may keep the value but it is no longer offered for new data.
slots.enumOption.icon: Icon name shown next to the member.
slots.enumOption.badge: Short badge text or color token shown next to the member.
slots.enumOption.description: A sentence describing what the member means.
slots.enumOption.help: Longer help shown when the user focuses the member.
slots.referenceDefinition.target: The referenced concept's name (`Concept`, or `pack::Concept` / `context::Concept` for one declared elsewhere).
slots.referenceDefinition.multiple: True: the field holds a list of references instead of one.
slots.referenceDefinition.displayField: Field of the target used as the human-readable text of a reference.
slots.referenceDefinition.lookupFields: Fields of the target shown in lookup results.
slots.referenceDefinition.searchFields: Fields of the target the picker searches when the user types.
slots.referenceDefinition.previewFields: Fields of the target shown in the hover or detail preview of a selected reference.
slots.referenceDefinition.displayTemplate: A template combining target fields into the displayed text, for example `{code} - {name}`.
slots.referenceDefinition.pickerColumns: Columns of the target shown in the picker dialog.
slots.referenceDefinition.previewCardTemplate: A template for the preview card shown for a selected reference.
slots.referenceDefinition.defaultFilter: A predicate that restricts which target rows the picker offers.
slots.referenceDefinition.inlineCreate: `allow` lets the user create a new target row from inside the picker; `deny` hides that option.
slots.referenceDefinition.via: Name of a field of the target to reference instead of its id. It must be the target's id or a unique field marked `connectable: anchor`.
slots.referenceDefinition.onDelete: What happens to this field when the referenced row is deleted: `restrict` refuses the delete, `cascade` deletes the referencing rows too, `nullify` clears the reference.
slots.schemaObject.type: The value type: a scalar field type, `object`, `array` or `reference`.
slots.schemaObject.scale: Digits after the decimal point of a decimal.
slots.schemaObject.minItems: Minimum number of elements of an array.
slots.schemaObject.maxItems: Maximum number of elements of an array.
slots.schemaObject.uniqueItems: True: array elements must all be different.
slots.schemaObject.itemIdentityField: Property that identifies an array element, used with `duplicationPolicy`.
slots.schemaObject.duplicationPolicy: `allow` or `deny` array elements that share the same identity.
slots.schemaObject.regex: A regular expression a string value must match.
slots.schemaObject.enumValues: The allowed values of an enum value.
slots.schemaObject.required: For an object, the names of the properties that must be present.
slots.schemaObject.properties: For an object, a map from property name to the `schemaObject` describing it.
slots.schemaObject.items: For an array, the `schemaObject` describing every element.
slots.schemaObject.defaultExpression: An expression giving the default value when none is supplied.
slots.schemaObject.derivedExpression: An expression that computes the value from its siblings.
slots.presentationMetadata.label: The user-facing name of the field or concept (plain string or per-locale object). Defaults to a prettified name.
slots.presentationMetadata.shortLabel: A shorter name used where space is tight, such as a table header or a mobile card.
slots.presentationMetadata.description: A sentence of help shown next to the control.
slots.presentationMetadata.placeholder: Hint text shown inside an empty input.
slots.presentationMetadata.helpText: Longer help text shown under the control.
slots.presentationMetadata.order: Position of the field in forms and details (lower first).
slots.presentationMetadata.widget: The control used to edit the field (for example `text`, `textarea`, `select`, `checkbox`, `date`, `number`, `custom`). It must be compatible with the field's type; the validator checks it. With `custom`, `customWidgetRef` names the component.
slots.presentationMetadata.group: Name of the group the field belongs to in a form; fields with the same group render together.
slots.presentationMetadata.section: Name of the form section (a titled block) the field is placed in.
slots.presentationMetadata.advanced: True: the field is tucked away under an Advanced toggle.
slots.presentationMetadata.deprecated: True: the field is kept for old data but hidden for new entries.
slots.presentationMetadata.visibleWhen: Expression over the record; the control is shown only while it is true.
slots.presentationMetadata.enabledWhen: Expression over the record; the control is editable only while it is true.
slots.presentationMetadata.readonlyWhen: Expression over the record; while true the control is read-only.
slots.presentationMetadata.requiredWhen: Expression over the record; while true the control is marked and enforced as required.
slots.presentationMetadata.pickerType: How a reference field is picked, for example a `search-dialog`.
slots.presentationMetadata.allowInlineCreate: True: the picker lets the user create a new target row in place.
slots.presentationMetadata.searchFields: Fields searched by the picker for this reference field.
slots.presentationMetadata.filterPreset: Name of a preset filter applied to the picker's candidate rows.
slots.presentationMetadata.tab: Name of the form tab the field is placed on.
slots.presentationMetadata.column: Grid column (1-based) the field occupies in a multi-column form.
slots.presentationMetadata.columnSpan: Number of grid columns the field spans in a multi-column form.
slots.presentationMetadata.width: Preferred width of the field's control or column (a CSS size or a keyword).
slots.presentationMetadata.summaryCard: True: the field is shown on the record's summary card.
slots.presentationMetadata.listColumn: True: the field is a column of the list; false hides it from the list.
slots.presentationMetadata.showInDefaultWebUi: False hides the field from the generated web UI entirely (it stays in the API).
slots.presentationMetadata.listColumnOrder: Position of the field among the list columns (lower first).
slots.presentationMetadata.formColumns: Concept-level. Number of columns of the create and edit form (default 1).
slots.presentationMetadata.displayMode: Concept-level. How the concept's records are shown by default, for example `standard`.
slots.presentationMetadata.formPresentation: Concept-level. `standard` (default) opens the create and edit form in place of the list with a Back to list action; `modal` opens it as a popup dialog.
slots.presentationMetadata.defaultSort: Concept-level. The field the list is sorted by by default.
slots.presentationMetadata.defaultGroup: Concept-level. An `enum` field whose members become the columns of the generated board (kanban) view; defaults to the lifecycle status field.
slots.presentationMetadata.imageField: On a reference field or concept: the field of the target that holds an image, shown as the thumbnail of a selected reference.
slots.presentationMetadata.customWidgetRef: With `widget: custom`: the relative path of the app-supplied widget component that renders the field.
slots.presentationMetadata.currency: ISO currency code (for example `BRL`) used to format a numeric field as money.
slots.conceptAccess.read: Expression evaluated per record that scopes which rows a caller may read; `$user.id`, `$user.tenantId`, `$user.roles` and the row's own fields are available. A row for which it is false is invisible.
slots.conceptAccess.write: Expression evaluated per record that scopes which rows a caller may change or delete.
slots.index.name: Name of the database index. Generated from the concept and fields when omitted.
slots.index.fields: The fields the index covers, in order. At least one.
slots.index.unique: True: the combination of the indexed fields must be unique.
slots.invariant.name: The rule's name, shown in the error when it is violated and used to refer to it from `override`.
slots.invariant.type: `unique` (the `fields` must be unique together) or `expression` (a boolean expression that must hold).
slots.invariant.specializes: Name of an inherited invariant this one refines.
slots.invariant.override: True: replaces the inherited invariant of the same name in a specializing concept.
slots.invariant.rule: A one-line rule text that the parser turns into the `type`, `fields` and `expression` of the invariant. Prefer the explicit keys.
slots.invariant.expression: The boolean expression over the row's fields that must be true for a write to be accepted.
slots.invariant.fields: For `type: unique`, the fields whose combined values must be unique.
slots.lifecycle.statusField: The enum field that stores the current state. Defaults to a field named `status`.
slots.lifecycle.states: The declared states, with labels, initial and terminal marks. When omitted they are derived from the transitions.
slots.lifecycle.transitions: The allowed moves between states, at least one. A move not listed here is refused.
slots.lifecycleState.value: The state's stored value (a member of the status field).
slots.lifecycleState.label: The text shown for the state.
slots.lifecycleState.initial: True: new rows start in this state.
slots.lifecycleState.allowedActions: Names of the actions offered while a row is in this state.
slots.lifecycleState.metadata: Free-form string notes about the state, carried into the compiled model unchanged.
slots.lifecycleTransition.event: Name of the event that triggers (and is published by) this transition.
slots.lifecycleTransition.guard: Expression over the row that must be true for the transition to be allowed.
slots.lifecycleTransition.actionLabel: Caption of the button that performs the transition.
slots.lifecycleTransition.action: Presentation of the transition's action (confirmation text, success message, danger level).
slots.lifecycleTransition.requiredPayload: Names of fields of the row that must hold a value for the transition to be performed.
slots.lifecycleTransition.metadata: Free-form string notes carried into the compiled model unchanged.
slots.actionMetadata.label: Caption of the action button.
slots.actionMetadata.confirmationText: Question shown for confirmation before the action runs.
slots.actionMetadata.successMessage: Message shown after the action succeeds.
slots.actionMetadata.failureHint: Hint shown to the user when the action fails.
slots.actionMetadata.dangerLevel: How destructive the action is: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `critical`; higher levels get stronger confirmation styling.
slots.actionMetadata.visibleWhen: Expression; the button is shown only while it is true.
slots.actionMetadata.permissionHint: Text explaining which permission the action needs.
slots.composition.collections: The aggregate's child collections, each loaded and saved with the root.
slots.composition.onCommit: Name of a procedure (or a flow of that name) that runs after the whole tree is written, in the same transaction; a failure rolls everything back.
slots.composition.metadata: Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged.
slots.aggregateCollection.name: The collection's name; its address inside the aggregate (nested ones are addressed `parent.child`).
slots.aggregateCollection.concept: The concept whose rows make up the collection.
slots.aggregateCollection.childField: Field of the child concept that points back to the parent row.
slots.aggregateCollection.ownership: `owned` (default): the aggregate creates and deletes the child rows. `referenced`: the rows exist independently and are only linked.
slots.aggregateCollection.orderBy: Field the collection's rows are ordered by.
slots.aggregateCollection.collections: Nested child collections (a second level, such as lines and their positions).
slots.fieldConvention.match: Which field names the rule types: an exact name (`name`) or a camelCase ending (`*Dt`). An ending matches when the field's LAST camelCase word is that text, so `*Name` matches `clientName` and `shippingAddressName` but not `name` (that is an exact rule) and not `hasToRename`. An exact rule beats an ending, a longer ending beats a shorter one.
slots.fieldConvention.defaults: What a matching field takes when it leaves the property out: always a `type`, optionally the size and constraint keys listed under it. A field that declares its own `type` is never touched.

inline.seed.repeatOver.vars: Index variables: a map from variable name to the inclusive integer range it takes.
inline.concept.rollups.field: The stored field of this concept that holds the aggregate.
inline.concept.rollups.from: The child concept whose rows are aggregated.
inline.concept.rollups.via: The field of the child concept that points at this concept.
inline.concept.rollups.fn: The aggregate function: count (default), sum, min, max or avg.
inline.concept.rollups.of: The child field the function applies to (not used by `count`).
inline.field.picker.multiSelect: True lets the user pick several rows.
inline.field.access.read: Expression evaluated per record; while false the field is hidden from the caller.
inline.field.access.write: Expression evaluated per record; while false the field is read-only for the caller.
inline.field.file.contentTypes: Allowed MIME types of the uploaded file.
inline.field.file.multiple: True: the field holds a list of files.
inline.conceptAccess.public.where: Filter narrowing which rows are public (the query `where` grammar; it cannot use `$user`). Absent means every row.
inline.conceptAccess.public.fields: The allow-list of fields served publicly (the id is always included).
inline.conceptAccess.public.scope: `concept` (default): the concept is publicly readable on its own. `aggregate`: its aggregate is served as a whole.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.type: The field type the rule gives: string, uuid, int, integer, long, decimal, boolean, date or datetime.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.maxLength: Longest text the field accepts; an explicit `maxLength` on the field wins.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.precision: Total digits of a decimal field (1 to 38).
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.scale: Digits after the decimal point of a decimal field.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.min: Smallest value a number field accepts.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.max: Largest value a number field accepts.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.required: Whether the field must be present.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.unique: Whether no two rows may share the value.
inline.fieldConvention.defaults.sensitive: Marks the field as sensitive (omitted from reads and logs unless granted).
